title: Introduce jurisdiction-aware assertion proxy, KMS consent router, and audit enrichment shim
author: Aisha Gupta
release_notes: Added an assertion proxy and KMS routing middleware to enable jurisdictional residency decisions and enriched audit headers; feature gated behind `jurisdiction_assertion` and rolled out with staged canary.
description: Motivation: customers with mixed-residency fleets asked for a deterministic place to evaluate operator/service jurisdiction assertions so KMS usage and audit provenance can be routed safely without sprinkling logic across services. This PR introduces an assertion proxy (service: residency-assertor) that normalizes incoming claims, evaluates configured jurisdiction policies, and emits a compact proof token used by downstream KMS routing and audit enrichment. It also adds a KMS Consent Router to pick an appropriate CMK/region and a lightweight audit-enrichment shim that attaches pseudonymous residency and proof metadata to audit events. Implementation summary: 1) residency-assertor service (new binary) with a small policy DSL converted into OPA-compatible JSON; 2) kms-consent-router middleware integrated into the existing kms-proxy client path with a decision cache and TTL; 3) audit-enricher sidecar that subscribes to commit log and augments events with residency_proof and audit_cohort tags; 4) feature flags and rollout controls (config path: /deploy/feature-flags/jurisdiction_assertion.json) and a canary rollout plan. Security and compliance notes: decisions compute a minimal proof (HMAC-signed) containing issuer, asserted_region, policy_id and exp; the HMAC key is stored in KMS and rotated via existing rotation pipeline; audit enrichment strips any direct tenant-identifiers and emits cohort hashes to maintain investigatability without exposing PII. Backwards compatibility: all services fall back to existing routing when the feature flag is off or residency-assertor returns no-decision. Performance: decision cache and async enrichment keep tail latency impact <5ms p95 on request path in our local benchmarks. Checklist: - [x] Policy DSL parser and unit tests - [x] kms-consent-router integrated and e2e tests - [x] audit-enricher implemented with audit schema migration + migration test harness - [x] Feature flag gating and canary rollout manifest - [x] Documentation: runbook + threat model note and operator guide - [x] Added telemetry: rbac_decisionlatencies, kms_routing_hits, audit_enrich_failures Rollout plan: staged canary to 5% tenants in region-us then 20% then global over two weeks; automated rollback triggers on >1% enrichment failures or >10% request-latency degradation. Related work: builds on ENG-991 (decision-cache) and SEC-88 (audit-envelope revamp). Links: linear/ENG-2345, internal-docs/ops/jurisdiction-rules. Testing: unit coverage 94% for new modules; integration pipeline added: unit -> lint -> e2e/kms-stub -> canary-simulation; CI transient: one flaky integration rerun but green on retry. Merge strategy and outcome: squash merge; post-merge migration job scheduled to backfill audit cohorts for 7 days. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to policy DSL escaping rules and HMAC key rotation path; reviewers asked to validate migration safety and to run the canary simulation tool locally.
